name: Ithran
overview: Ithran was a male member of the tribe of Asher, identified specifically as the son of Zophah. Beyond this genealogical detail, Scripture does not provide additional notes or narrative about him. His mention is brief and primarily genealogical in nature.
namesAndTitles: The name Ithran means 'what is over, profit; excellent,' reflecting a positive and honorable meaning in Hebrew. He is also referred to as Jether in a related verse, though no specific meaning is given for this name in Scripture. Neither name is indicated as being divinely given.
familyAndRelationships: Ithran is explicitly recorded as the son of Zophah. Inferred from the genealogical context are his descendants or related family members Jephunneh, Pispa, and Ara, who are noted as his sons. Scripture does not provide additional family details beyond these relationships.
scriptureSignificance: Ithran's significance lies in his place within the genealogical records of the tribe of Asher, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 7. His mention as the son of Zophah and father to notable descendants establishes his role in the lineage and tribal history important for understanding the heritage of Israel. Such genealogies underscore God's providential preservation of His people through generations.
